result:
No failures (the warnings are pre-existing, unrelated controllers).

`PostController.update()` was hand-rolling its response as `new Response(null, { status: 302, headers: { Location: ... } })`. Because the edit form submits with `PUT`, a 302 tells the browser to re-issue the *same* method against the redirect target — so it looped `PUT /posts/:id` until `ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS`, after the update had already been written (hence the saved-but-stuck symptom); `store()` and `destroy()` were unaffected only because they already went through the framework helper. I replaced it with `return this.redirect(\`/posts/${post.id}\`)` in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:96`, which emits 303 See Other for non-GET requests and makes the browser follow up with a plain GET of the post page, matching the post-publish behaviour; validation still throws before the redirect, so 422 responses on the edit form are untouched. I added `tests/PostUpdate.test.ts` covering both paths — a successful save returns 303 with `Location: /posts/<id>` and persists the new title, and an empty payload still returns 422. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (4 tests across 3 files) both pass.
